title: Chapter 679
paragraphs: Chapter 679
Episode 173. Chasing the Sword (4)
Vamel Alliance, Sword's Garden, Zipple, and Kinzelo.
I never imagined that all of them would end up entering Temar's sixth tomb together.
From the possibility of meeting a living old Runcandel, to the flight of the sword, to the current situation.
This tomb opening was far beyond expectations in every aspect.
Hoooooo...!
The aura continuously emerging from the sword was causing a huge whirlpool.
The sword was hidden under the sea water, but structures and some sort of devices were rising from the seabed as time passed.
Ruined ramparts, broken turrets, and unidentified devices that looked like defensive equipment. The subspace within the sword seemed to have been damaged several times; it was not normal.
Yet, an unknown sense of crisis was chilling Jin's neck.
‘Is it because of the Guardian?'
Except for when he met the person, Ruet Damirow Yul, a living old Runcandel, who he ‘cannot remember,’ Jin often found himself in crisis every time he opened a tomb.
This time too, signals of danger were coming from his whole body. The source of that signal was not from the pursuit team sent by the Sword's Garden, but precisely from the seabed.
‘The aura used to open the tomb has been fully restored during the journey, so there's no issue in the battle.’
It was decided to rule out the assumption that the Guardian will correctly identify friends and foes.
It's likely to indiscriminately attack, and it seemed better to take advantage of this to first get rid of the enemies.
‘The problem lies with Zipple and Kinzelo. To what extent should I protect them…’
Jin, who was thinking up to there, shook his head.
‘They are not kids. There's no need for me to worry about them.’

If they thought it was an important issue, they would have sent the appropriate personnel themselves. If it were an issue of temporary alliance, they would have requested support in advance, but this was more of a personal issue for Jin.
In a sense, those guys are those who poked their noses into personal matters, so although there was no need to harm them, there was no need to actively protect them either.

‘Anyway, I can feel the energy of Bianca Caligo and Ranke Halobich from Kinzelo’s side, so even if Zephyrin can’t use his power, they will protect themselves. On Zipple's side, Kadun is under treatment, so Octavia and Ronil would have come, but they are not ones incapable of taking care of themselves.’
Ships and dragons from the Sword's Garden, Zipple, and Kinzelo were getting closer. Jin aimed in the direction where Chaos Dragon and Black Line were and shot a Light Speed Stab.
As the Light Speed Stab, containing lightning energy, rushed in, the charging Chaos Dragon and Black Line oxidized, leaving remnants of chaos.
The sea turning over as if creating a new world, the brilliant energy emitted by the forces of each faction, and in the center of that, a single sword thrust into the ground.
While all of this was unfolding like a scene from a myth, the Guardian was finally revealing itself from the seabed.
No, Guardians.
"Master, there are giant beings at the seabed...!"
Jin looked down.
Red eyes, ominous like a distant wildfire, were looking up at the intruders.
Huge bodies like castles, a giant spear and shield to match. The giants, shaped like humans, seemed to be carved out of a hard rock that not even Jin could easily cut.
Apart from Jin and Hedo, everyone else was on the verge of freezing due to the overwhelming pressure.
It wasn't just one or two.
Over a hundred giants seemed to be preparing to slaughter the intruders.
Moreover, their numbers were increasing in real-time, not popping out from buildings or underground, but forming a short while after their outlines became visible in the air.
[Those are... Graveyard Giants?]
Quicantel swallowed with a gasp.
Graveyard Giants.
It was an ancient weapon that once nearly endangered the youngest division back when Jin was a Life Vessel.
At the time, the threat to the youngest division had been the work of Bubbar Gaston, and Murakan had suppressed it in a single go.

'At that point, Murakan hadn't regained much of his strength. Even if there was only one of those, it should have been impossible to suppress it, but is it different because that was Bubbar's work and these are originals?'
However, looking at Quicantel's expression, it didn't seem to be that.
"Quicantel, do you know about them?"
Valkas asked.

[Of course, we dragons killed all the remaining Graveyard Giants two thousand years ago. It was a war in which Murakan and I participated. However, these Graveyard Giants are a different kind from those we defeated.]
-God of Sculpture, Wel? It's a name I'm hearing for the first time.
-It's natural that you don't know. Like Clam we met in Colon, he's one of the gods who disappeared from history. They say Wel has been in the tomb of the dead gods.
The past conversation about Murakan and the Graveyard Giants.
According to the dragons, the Graveyard Giants are weapons created by the 'God of Sculpture, Wel'. Created to protect himself, who had fallen to an ordinary human, and the forgotten tomb of the gods.
Quicantel's face twisted.
[A little while ago, Aria mentioned that this tomb doesn't seem to be Solderet's subspace, right?]
"Yes, because Solderet's name was not indicated in the record window."
[It seems that this is not Temar but a tomb of a dead god. And it would be different from the tomb we dragons handled.]
"So, it might originally be a tomb of a dead god, but it could have been used temporarily as Temar's tomb during the process of being repurposed."
"Perhaps that's the case... Ugh!"
Suddenly, Quicantel shook her head as if in pain, just as she had when she reacted to her forgotten memory manipulated by Murakan.
[The tenth knight who chose to guard this place... he was a person related to the dead god who originally owned this tomb...!]
Remembering more was too much. Quicantel took a deep breath to regain her senses.
"We should meet him and ask. About the stories intertwined with this tomb."
"The fact that Quicantel's memory is starting to come back is evidence that there's an old Runcandel alive in here, Jin."
At Valeria's words, Jin nodded.
"It's a big harvest, Keeper. I have a favor to ask."
"You're shameless. It's getting worse, and in this crisis, you're asking me for a favor?"
"I will handle all the Graveyard Giants myself. So instead of just protecting Sandra, please look after my colleagues too."
"No, I will leave as soon as I find the sword."
Jin, shaking his head as if sorry,
"If that's possible, do so. But I can read the spirit energy, and that sword is firmly fixed so that no one can pull it out right now."
Jin pointed to the sword as he spoke.
It wasn't a lie.
Jin was sure that even if he used all his spirit energy again, he couldn't pull out Hedo's sword stuck in the seabed.
Moreover, the sword was no longer in the peculiarly long shape that Hedo knew.
"My... sword, what is that bizarre shape!"
"Perhaps that's the original form of the sword you have."
Valeria shrugged her shoulders and answered for Jin.
It would be apt to describe the blade as having horns.
Hedo, who heightened his sense of sight, was gritting his teeth, looking at the small blades that sprouted on both sides of the sword blade.
"12th Baaaaaaaah!"
In the end, Hedo exploded and screamed.
He had been through situations that worsened like this before, but it was the first time since he met Sandra.
No matter what crazy things Sandra did, there had never been a situation where Hedo couldn't control it.
It was impossible for Hedo to give up on the sword and escape for now.

At the minimum, the subspace formed in the sea is about ten miles in size. Since it's in the middle of the sea, it's impossible to run out, and above all, the layers of spirit energy curtains were a problem.
The curtain seemed to not disappear unless it swallowed all the intruders.
Some of the people from the Sword Garden and Gyp already got sucked into the curtain, leaving behind screams of despair.
There was no need to even imagine what happened to those who were absorbed into the curtain. Flesh, swords, and debris like staffs were pouring out from the opposite surface where they were caught.
This place was already hell.
"I'm genuinely sorry. Given the situation, I can only suggest the best possible direction. I will definitely apologize and compensate when this is over."
Jin wanted to apologize more properly, but he ended briefly as the Graveyard Giants began to move.
"Quicantel, Valkas, Keeper, I entrust my colleagues to you. Let's handle this as quickly as possible."
"Hey, Hedo! He's trying to go alone against those monsters, throw yourself in and help too!"
"Ugh, grrrrr!"
While Hedo was making strange noises trying to hold onto his sanity, Valeria grabbed Jin's shoulder.
"I'm going down too, Jin Runcandel."
"What!? Why are you!?"
Of course, that was Sandra's reaction, not Jin's.
The other colleagues also felt strange.
It's hard to understand why Valeria would join a fight that even Valkas can't participate in.
But Jin followed her words without hesitation.
"I'd appreciate it."
If it were her previous life, it might be different, but Valeria now is not the type to rush to her doom because Jin is worried.
So her stepping forward meant she was confident.
Valeria naturally held out her hand to Jin.
With no particular meaning, just to descend together for the battle, but Sandra had no choice but to feel like her blood was boiling.
"This, this. This pair... what are you doing! Stop, stop! Ah, dizz, dizziness!"
"Miss!"
In the end, Sandra passed out as if she couldn't bear to see that scene (Hedo took care of Sandra even in the midst of this), and Jin took Valeria's hand.
It was the hand of his teacher that he held after a long time.
Could he share the heavy burdens contained in this thin and frail hand in this life? No, perhaps he is already sharing.
Jin suddenly had that thought.
"Go."
When Jin and Valeria jumped off Quicantel's back, the Graveyard Giants shot crimson beams as if they had been waiting.
Jin's aura and Valeria's blue magic intertwined and illuminated the dark seabed.
Jin felt the sense of crisis that had made his neck cold when the subspace first opened, quickly fading away.
